title: Verne Robotics' V0.5 Robot Model Can Learn New Industrial Tasks in Under 2 Hours
summary:
The robotics startup's latest AI framework specializes in rapid skill acquisition for industrial automation, allowing robots to adapt to unfamiliar factory workflows using minimal training. Technical details released for the V0.5 open-weight model show that it can acquire new industrial tasks from less than 2 hours of demonstrations. Trained on more than 1.7M demonstrations using the Wan2.2 video generator, V0.5 outperformed a rival model in environmental stability tests; when faced with randomized clutter and lighting on the RoboTwin 2.0 benchmark, V0.5's success rate fell to 73.4%, while Physical Intelligence's π0.5 dropped from 70.7% to 46.0%.

Verne is now scaling its training data 10x after finding that increasing pretraining data without task-specific fine-tuning increased the model's benchmark success rate from 23% to 51%. To ensure reliability in industrial settings, the model runs inference directly on the robot hardware to remove the need for constant cloud connectivity or high-speed Wi-Fi. The company has published the weights and inference code for V0.5 on Huggingface.

selectedTweets.text:
Brilliant release by @VerneRobotics

V0.5, an open-weight world action model, that looks through cameras and outputs the next second of arm, gripper and mobile-base motion. 

The big deal is that it learned new industrial tasks from under 2 hours of demonstrations.

> Robot models usually stumble when a room changes. With clutter and new lighting that neither model trained on, Verne Robotics’ V0.5 lost 7.6 points in simulation, while Physical Intelligence’s π0.5 lost 24.7.

> On RoboTwin 2.0, randomized clutter, lighting and textures cut V0.5 from 81.0% to 73.4% in Verne’s tests, while Physical Intelligence’s π0.5 fell from 70.7% to 46.0%.

> Built on the Wan2.2 video generator, V0.5 learned from over 1.7M demonstrations to predict upcoming camera frames alongside the motion producing them.

selectedTweets.bestBit: V0.5 trains on two objectives at once: predicting the robot’s next actions and predicting what its cameras will see next.
selectedTweets.text:
V0.5 trains on two objectives at once: predicting the robot’s next actions and predicting what its cameras will see next.

The video prediction is only there to teach the model how scenes change. 

At runtime, V0.5 outputs actions directly, so the policy gets a world model’s scene understanding without generating video on every control step.
